1. (Currently amended) A method comprising: a processor determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; the processor accessing a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; the processor receiving an indication from the data store that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication with respect to at least one of the payment transactions; the processor accepting the received indication as proof-of-life with respect to the recipient; and the processor making the benefit payment to the recipient in response to said proof-of-life, wherein the method includes at least one additional technological step beyond the abstract idea of authenticating a recipient and making a payment, comprising: the processor analyzing biometric authentication data from payment transaction records to verify recipient identity and liveness through recent transaction history.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said at least one payment transaction occurred during a pre-determined period of time prior to said accessing step, and wherein the processor uses the time-based verification of recent biometric authentication as a technological measure to reduce fraud risk in benefit payment distribution.

3. (Previously presented) The method of claim 2, wherein said pre-determined period of time is seven days.

4. (Previously presented) The method of claim 2, wherein said pre-determined period of time is 24 hours.

5. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment.

6. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the at least one of the payment transactions includes a credit card account transaction and/or a debit card account transaction.

7. (Previously presented) The method of claim 6, wherein a mobile device was used by the recipient to initiate the at least one payment transaction.

8. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is made via an electronic monetary transfer to an account owned by the recipient.

9. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is made by sending a check to the recipient.

10. (Currently amended) A method comprising: a processor determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; the processor accessing, at a first point in time, a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; the processor determining that the data store contains an indication that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication most recently with respect to one of said payment transactions at a second point in time earlier than the first point in time; the processor comparing a time interval defined by the second and first points in time with a pre-determined permissive time interval; the processor making the benefit payment, without requiring proof-of-life authentication of the recipient, in a case where the time interval defined by the second and first points in time does not exceed the pre-determined permissive time interval; and the processor requiring proof-of-life authentication of the recipient, prior to making the benefit payment, in a case where the time interval defined by the second and first points in time exceeds the pre-determined permissive time interval, wherein the method includes at least one additional technological step beyond the abstract idea of authenticating a recipient and making a payment, comprising: the processor implementing a time-based verification system that uses biometric authentication records from payment transactions as a technological measure to automatically determine benefit payment eligibility and reduce fraud risk.

11. (Previously presented) The method of claim 10, wherein the pre-determined permissive time interval is seven days.

12. (Previously presented) The method of claim 10, wherein the pre-determined permissive time interval is 24 hours.

13. (Previously presented) The method of claim 10, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment.

14. (Currently amended) An apparatus comprising: a processor; and a memory in communication with the processor, the memory storing program instructions, the processor operative with the program instructions to perform functions as follows: the processor determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; the processor accessing a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; the processor receiving an indication from the data store that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication with respect to at least one of the payment transactions; the processor accepting the received indication as proof-of-life with respect to the recipient; and the processor making the benefit payment to the recipient in response to said proof-of-life, wherein the apparatus includes at least one additional technological component beyond abstract authentication and payment processing, comprising: a biometric verification module configured to analyze authentication data from payment transaction records to verify recipient identity and liveness through recent transaction history.

15. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein said at least one payment transaction occurred during a pre-determined period of time prior to said accessing, and wherein the biometric verification module uses time-based verification of recent biometric authentication as a technological measure to reduce fraud risk in benefit payment distribution.

16. (Previously presented) The apparatus of claim 15, wherein said pre-determined period of time is seven days.

17. (Previously presented) The apparatus of claim 15, wherein said pre-determined period of time is 24 hours.

18. (Previously presented) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment.

19. (Previously presented) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein the at least one of the payment transactions includes a credit card account transaction and/or a debit card account transaction.

20. (Previously presented) The apparatus of claim 19, wherein a mobile device was used by the recipient to initiate the at least one payment transaction.
